newsitem.title: RUSSIA: GM, Ukraine still considering car venture. [CORRECTED 01:15 GMT 03/12]
newsitem.headline: GM, Ukraine still considering car venture. [CORRECTED 01:15 GMT 03/12]

text.p: General Motors Corp, which Ukraine recently demoted from preferred partner status in a planned venture with car plant AvtoZAZ, said on Friday the U.S. firm was not looking for other investment options in Ukraine.

Greg DeYonker, executive vice president of GM Overseas Corp, met Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko on November 14 and reaffirmed the goals of their relationship, DeYonker said. (Corrects to make clear that official met was Prime Minister Lazarenko and not President Leonid Kuchma.)
In late October Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko reversed an earlier decision to back only GM as a potential partner for AT AvtoZAZ after GM had taken on a $500,000 feasibility study.
Other foreign carmakers, including South Korea's Daewoo, have been interested in the plant, which builds the Tavria mid-range car.
But DeYonker said in a telephone interview from Switzerland that GM was "not at this point" looking for other investment options.

"We (Kuchma and DeYonker) reaffirmed that we have a joint understanding just to complete the feasibility study by the end fo the year and then to sit down and analyse whether an investment in Ukraine makes sense."
GM has begun investing a total of $200-$250 million in Russia's Tatarstan to fit out a factory which will produce 50,000 Blazer luxury off-road vehicles.
